cases.title: 'Do the rest' before any demo is the ask: the one demo runs, the rest handed back in one sentence, no later offer

rubric.reason: In Turn 3 the learner asked "Can you just stagger the rest for me?" before any demo. The mentor ran the one offset_demo on Dot 2 and said "I shifted all of Dot 2's keys later by your 4 frames... Edit > Undo reverses it." It handed back "Dot 3 is yours to stagger. Play it back and say done." There was no repeated how-to and no offer to do more; the blank-frame remark is a fixture artifact and is ignored.

Turn 3 describes the one change in plain words with real names ("I shifted all of Dot 2's keys later by your 4 frames, so it now starts after Dot 1"). That matches the tool result. It says "Edit > Undo reverses it" with no undo label or field names, and it hands Dot 3 back without offering to do it.

Turn 1 ends on the choice ("Do you want to stagger Dot 2's properties, or the three Dots?"). Turn 2 carries the lockstep sentence and frame as context, says the plan back and gives the how-to with keys, bar and Quick Offset as alternatives, then ends on "Play it back and say done." Turn 3 is the demo turn and ends on Dot 3 handed back. Turn 4 names the pair still together and ends on a step for the learner. No turn is a lecture or ends with nothing to do.
